_note: Nationwide scenic train views, the catalogue behind the homepage view picker. Only status 'live' is shown to readers. Everything else is a candidate: which side, which section and which season are left null until verified (viewshed from OpenStreetMap track geometry + GSI elevation, then checked against real footage). Never publish a side that has not been verified — one wrong 'sit on the right' costs the whole site's credibility. Images are generated (illustrative) and labelled as such wherever shown.

views.name: The sea (Sagami Bay)
views.season: All year; the sun sets over the sea in the late afternoon
views.basis: terrain model only: open water within 250 m of the track

notes: Enoden cars have long bench seats along the sides. To face the sea, sit on the land-side bench, or stand by the sea-side windows; the cab window at the front of the train works too.

On clear days Mt. Fuji and Enoshima show over the sea from the same stretch — behind you going to Kamakura, ahead going to Fujisawa. The terrain model shows both; they are not given a side because they sit ahead of or behind the train, not to one side.
routes.verification: Side and section from a terrain model (GSI elevation, OSM track), counting the sea as a view only where open water lies within 250 m of the line, because buildings are not modelled. No seat letters: the cars have bench seats.

routes.title: The Hayakawa valley and three switchbacks on the Hakone Tozan Railway
routes.season: All year; hydrangeas June–July, autumn leaves in November

osm.name: 小田急箱根鉄道線|箱根登山鉄道鉄道線|箱根登山線

image.alt: Hydrangeas in bloom beside the track through the window of a red mountain train

routes.teaser: Hakone · the valley side, through three switchbacks
routes.evidence: Hakone day trips from Tokyo; the line is a sight in itself.

timing.source: Station timetables of the Hakone Tozan Railway on hakonenavi.jp (the operator group’s official site), weekdays, read November 2026: the 13:12 from Hakone-Yumoto and the 13:08 from Gora, followed station by station. Gora arrival taken as 2 minutes after Chokoku-no-Mori and Hakone-Yumoto arrival as 4 minutes after Tonosawa (the published runs the other way). Between stops, spread by distance along the track.

views.name: The Hayakawa valley, below Ohiradai
views.basis: terrain model only: the ground falls away up to about 120 m on that side

views.name: The Hayakawa valley, Miyanoshita to Gora
views.season: All year; autumn leaves in November
views.basis: terrain model only: the ground falls away up to about 150 m on that side

notes: The train reverses three times on the way up — at Deyama, at Ohiradai station and at Kami-Ohiradai — and the driver and conductor change ends each time. Sides on this page are for the direction of travel, so they flip at each reversal; the side of the car does not. Going up from Hakone-Yumoto, the valley side is the left side of the car as you board, nearly all the way. Coming down from Gora, it is also the left as you board.
Between Tonosawa and Deyama the line crosses the Hayakawa on the Deyama bridge, high above the river: a view from both sides, gone in seconds.

Woods line much of the track. The model finds where the ground falls away on one side, not where the trees open; the view comes and goes through the leaves. Hydrangeas grow on both sides in June and July.
routes.verification: Side and sections from a terrain model (GSI 10 m elevation, OSM track followed rail by rail through the switchbacks): the valley counts as in view where the ground falls 40 m or more within 400 m on one side and no nearer bank hides it. No published source was found for the side, so it rests on the model alone. No seat letters.

page.title: Hakone Tozan Railway: Which Side for the Valley, Through Three Switchbacks?
page.description: Hakone-Yumoto to Gora: the train reverses three times, so left and right keep flipping — but the Hayakawa valley stays on the left side of the car as you board. A terrain model, a map and the minutes from the official timetable.

views.name: The Hozu gorge, Arashiyama to Hozukyo
views.season: Autumn leaves mid-November to early December; cherry blossom early April
views.basis: terrain model, matching a published description (All About): the river 10–35 m below on that side

views.name: The Hozu gorge, Hozukyo to Kameoka
views.season: Autumn leaves mid-November to early December; cherry blossom early April
views.basis: terrain model, matching a published description (All About): the river 10–30 m below on that side

notes: The line crosses the river near Torokko Hozukyo, so the gorge switches sides: on the left from Arashiyama to Hozukyo, then on the right to Kameoka, going from Saga — the longer stretch. Coming back from Kameoka it is the other way round: on the left most of the way, then on the right after Hozukyo.

Every seat is reserved, on facing wooden benches, so your side depends on the seat you are given. If you can choose, take the right side going to Kameoka (the left coming back) for the longer stretch, and look across for the rest.
The current trains run until 29 December 2026. New cars start on 1 March 2027, when times and fares may change — we will update this page then.
routes.verification: Side and sections from a terrain model (GSI 10 m elevation, OSM track followed rail by rail): the gorge counts as in view where the ground falls 10 m or more to the river within 200 m on one side and no nearer bank hides it. The order — left first, then right after the crossing near Hozukyo — matches All About’s published account; one other guide gives the halves the other way round. No seat letters.

page.title: Sagano Romantic Train: Which Side for the Hozu Gorge?
page.description: Torokko Saga to Kameoka: the Hozu river is on the left as far as Hozukyo, then on the right — the longer stretch — all the way to Kameoka. A terrain model, a map and the minutes from the 2026 timetable.

timing.source: Yurikamome station timetables (yurikamome.co.jp), weekdays, read November 2026: the 22:32 from Shimbashi and the 22:44 from Toyosu, followed station by station. Run times checked against the next train each way (22:40 and 22:53), which match minute for minute; trains run every 3–8 minutes through the day. Toyosu and Shimbashi arrivals taken as the published run the other way (1 minute). Between stops, spread by distance along the track.

views.season: All year; the bridge is lit after dark
views.basis: terrain model only: open water at least 400 m across, within 300 m of the line

views.name: The Odaiba waterfront
views.season: All year; sunset over the harbour in the late afternoon
views.basis: terrain model only: open water at least 400 m across, within 300 m of the line

views.name: The Harumi waterfront and the city
views.season: All year; city lights after dark
views.basis: terrain model only: open water at least 400 m across, within 300 m of the line

notes: After Shibaura-futo the line climbs a full circle onto the Rainbow Bridge, then crosses it on the lower deck: water on both sides, the city behind you going to Odaiba. On the loop the view swings round, so it is not given a side.
The line has no driver. The seats at the very front (and back) of the train look straight down the track — the best view of the loop and the bridge, if you can get them.

Buildings are not in the model, and in Tokyo they hide much of the water. We only count open water at least 400 m across that comes within 300 m of the line, so canals do not count — but a warehouse or a hotel can still stand in the way.
Cars mostly have long bench seats along the sides.
routes.verification: Side and sections from a terrain model (GSI elevation, where water has no height; OSM track followed rail by rail through the loop): the bay counts as in view where open water at least 400 m across comes within 300 m of the line on one side. No published source was found for the sides, so they rest on the model alone. No seat letters.

page.description: Shimbashi to Toyosu: Tokyo Bay is on the left from Takeshiba, the loop and the Rainbow Bridge have water on both sides, then the Odaiba waterfront is on the right. A terrain model, a map and the minutes from the official timetable.
